mini.title: Art
mini.passage: Shape is two-dimensional; form occupies or suggests three dimensions. Proportion compares parts with each other or a whole. Artists may use realistic or intentionally altered proportions.

items.prompt: How do shape and form differ?
items.answer: Shape is flat; form has or suggests depth.

items.prompt: Sketch a body-system or object diagram and compare two proportions using number or ratio skills. Use a labeled drawing and 3-5 sentences.
items.answer: Look for a relevant completed activity, an accurate concept, evidence or an example, and a reasoned explanation/revision. Accept varied justified responses. Do not grade beliefs or private experiences.

mini.title: Life Sciences
mini.passage: Attention selects some information for processing. Distractions compete for attention. A fair comparison keeps tasks similar and changes one feature; one trial cannot establish a rule about everyone.

items.prompt: What should stay similar in a fair comparison?
items.answer: The task difficulty, length, timing, and instructions.

items.prompt: Compare recall of similar short lists with and without a harmless distraction; repeat and identify limits. Use a labeled drawing and 3-5 sentences.
items.answer: Look for a relevant completed activity, an accurate concept, evidence or an example, and a reasoned explanation/revision. Accept varied justified responses. Do not grade beliefs or private experiences.

mini.passage: Memory involves encoding, storing, and retrieving information. Grouping material and recalling it without looking can support learning. Forgetting does not establish that someone is incapable.

items.prompt: How can grouping help recall?
items.answer: It organizes information and supplies meaningful retrieval cues.

items.prompt: Recall five familiar objects; repeat using meaningful groups and compare strategies. Use a labeled drawing and 3-5 sentences.

mini.passage: Animals need species-appropriate food, water, shelter, exercise, and health care. Follow adult-approved care plans rather than guessing. Wash hands after appropriate animal-care tasks.

mini.title: Life Sciences
mini.passage: Emotions provide information about experiences but do not establish facts about other people. Naming a feeling and pausing can help a person choose a response. People may experience the same event differently.

items.prompt: Can people feel differently about the same event?
items.answer: Yes; their experiences and interpretations can differ.

mini.passage: A file stores information; folders organize files. Clear names and predictable locations make work easier to find. Save copies before major changes and check where downloads go.
